elements.element: Preferred: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 90 days' written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Preferred: pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund language; instead "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Preferred: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "HDI may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term, upon 90 days' written notice" (a Vendor convenience right exists)

elements.element: Fallback: Customer termination for convenience on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 90 days' written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Fallback: early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "provided the Termination Payment shall not exceed 3 months' fees"

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor convenience termination only at the end of a term
elements.evidence: "HDI may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term"

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor convenience termination on 90 days' notice

reasons: All four atomic fallback elements are operative: a Customer convenience right at 90 days (within the 60–90 day band), a cap on the Termination Payment at 3 months' fees, and an HDI convenience right confined to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.

Preferred fails on three independent elements: notice is 90 rather than 30 days, there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and HDI retains a (limited) convenience right rather than none during a committed term. Consistent with the locked fallback target.

Minimality holds: two surgical edits — one concise insertion supplying the absent convenience-termination mechanic, and a short proviso appended to the existing Termination Payment formula rather than a rewrite of 4.2(a). The bracketed gloss 'for this purpose "Customer" means the Company' is a necessary alias bridge because the agreement names the customer 'the Company', so it is not surplus.

Intent preserved: the one-year term, automatic renewal, either-party 90-day non-renewal notice, the Net Sales-based Termination Payment formula and the eight-quarterly-instalment payment mechanic in 4.2(c) all remain effective; the new proviso only caps, and does not displace, the formula.

Noted in rationale only (not a deviation): 'fees' is not a defined term in this Net Sales-based agreement, so the cap would read more cleanly tied to a defined revenue/fee metric; and the preferred pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts was not obtained.
